problem:
What is the standard deviation of the following data set?

$$
1,\,1,\,5,\,4,\,9
$$
worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a data set ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is the square root of the variance:

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2}}=\sqrt{\,\,\,\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-{(\overset{―}{x})}^{2}}
$$

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=5$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (1+1+5+4+9) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot 20 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot ({1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{9}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (1+1+25+16+81) \\  & =\frac{124}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{124}{5}-{(4)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{124}{5}-16 \\  & =\frac{124-80}{5} \\  & =\frac{44}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the standard deviation is

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{44}{5}}.
$$
